name: Reddish Chestnut
lede: Reddish Chestnut is ColorHub's English name for Su'ōkō, a muted brick red that Japanese tradition names for the smoky, perfumed scent of sappanwood incense, not for a tree.

sections.title: An incense, not a nut
sections.body:
Wikipedia's list of traditional Japanese colors gives this swatch as Su'ōkō (蘇芳香), combining suō, the sappanwood dye also used for a family of red-brown colors, with kō, "incense" or "fragrance," naming a red tied to scent rather than sight alone [1]. ColorHub's English rendering, Reddish Chestnut, substitutes a tree and a nut for an aromatic wood dye [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 places the swatch in block 15, "moderate red," about 5.5 units from that block's centre [2]. The library's nearest other named color is [[pompeian-red]], 2.6 units away [2].

Measured in LCH it reads lightness 44, chroma 40, hue 33 degrees, a moderately bright, warm brick red [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in 365 of 23,781 paintings, under 2 percent, as photographed [3]. It plays a mid-tone role in 62 percent of its occurrences [3]. Fra Angelico and Henri Matisse each carry it at nine times or more the archive's overall rate [3]. It shares canvases more than chance with the simple color word Red, at nearly 30 times the ordinary rate, and its presence peaks in the 1400s, in 47 of 945 paintings [3].

origin.named_after: the sappanwood dye, by way of its incense (kō)
origin.first_recorded: undocumented in English; traditional Japanese usage
